search_log: Searched “The Devil's Advocate” “Morris West” with excerpt, first chapter, narrator, point of view, first person, third person, omniscient, epistolary, and alternating-narration terms.
Opened and inspected the authorized Allen & Unwin excerpt hosted by AbeBooks and the Allen & Unwin ebook preview on Everand.

Searched exact first-person quotations to distinguish base narration from speech; the Kochi Reading Group passages explicitly place q00733 and q00734 in Meredith’s dialogue and reproduce numerous third-person interior scenes.

Checked Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive records; Google Books offered mainly snippets and contents, while the Internet Archive editions required borrowing and supplied no usable open text.
Targeted searches found no credible evidence of sustained first-person, second-person, epistolary, or alternating base sections.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, with mobile focalization among Meredith, Meyer, Nina, Nerone, and others. Diagnostic quotes q00742 and q00746 agree with the authorized opening, which externally narrates multiple characters and their thoughts. The numerous first-person quotations are character speech, reflection, or report; web context directly confirms this for Meredith’s prayer passage, and no source indicates that such passages form autonomous first-person sections. The main limitation is that the strongest authorized prose is from the opening, but substantial interior and late-book passages corroborate the same third-person structure, with no credible contrary evidence.
